bridge_metadata.title: DDR-Neuro Bridge
bridge_metadata.subtitle: DNA damage response genes with neurological phenotypes — a bridge from the CicciaLab genetic interaction map to neuroprotection

source_article.citation: Hayward et al., Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response. Nature Biotechnology 2026.

source_database.name: CicciaLab DDR Genetic Interactions Database
source_database.institution: Ciccia Laboratory, Columbia University Medical Center
source_database.license_note: No explicit open-data license stated; copyright Ciccia Lab. This bridge page curates neuro-relevant gene-disease associations from public sources (OMIM, ClinVar) and links to the database for full interaction data. It does not redistribute the interaction matrix.

bridge_metadata.curation_method: DDR genes with established neurological phenotypes (OMIM/Genetics Home Reference) cross-referenced against the 233-gene CicciaLab screen scope. Phenotype annotations are from public medical genetics resources.

featured_interaction_pairs.source: Hayward et al. 2026 (article abstract, publicly described)
featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: Both genes have emerging roles in neuronal DNA damage tolerance; synthetic lethality suggests a therapeutic window in tumors but also flags double-hit vulnerability in neurons.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: None yet mapped; candidate target for future neuroprotection compound screens.

featured_interaction_pairs.complex_b: FANCM Fanconi anemia M / replication fork
featured_interaction_pairs.source: Hayward et al. 2026 (article abstract, publicly described)
featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: SMARCAL1 mutations cause Schimke immuno-osseous dysplasia with CNS manifestations; FANCM is in the Fanconi anemia pathway with established neurodevelopmental impact.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: PARP inhibitors (approved) target synthetic lethal partners of HR-deficient backgrounds; FANCM-deficient backgrounds may be similarly targetable.

featured_interaction_pairs.source: Established DDR literature (Fanconi-BRCA pathway cross-talk); confirmed in CicciaLab database.
featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: Buffering interactions reveal functional redundancy — a compound that inhibits one may be rescued by the other. Critical context for neuroprotection compound design in Fanconi backgrounds.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: PARP inhibitors exploit loss of HR; FANCD2-BRCA2 buffering is the resistance mechanism to target.

featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: Both genes cause Cockayne syndrome with severe neurodegeneration. Their buffering relationship (shared transcription-coupled repair function) explains the phenotypic overlap.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: No current neuroprotection compounds target NER directly; candidate for natural product screens focused on oxidative stress (ROS is the neurotoxic driver in CS neurons).

featured_interaction_pairs.source: Established DDR literature; ATM-TP53 synthetic lethality is the rationale for TP53-deleted RPE-1 cell line in the CicciaLab screen.
featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: ATM mutations cause ataxia-telangiectasia (cerebellar neurodegeneration). The TP53-deleted screening context is itself a model for how DDR context shapes neuronal vulnerability.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: ATM inhibitors (KU-55933 and analogs) are research tools; natural product screens for ATM-pathway modulators are an open frontier.

featured_interaction_pairs.source: Aicardi-Goutières syndrome literature; both cause AGS via cytosolic nucleic acid sensing.
featured_interaction_pairs.neuro_relevance_note: Both genes cause Aicardi-Goutières syndrome — a devastating pediatric neuroinflammatory disorder. The interaction highlights that DDR genes can drive neurodegeneration via innate immune activation, not just failed repair.
featured_interaction_pairs.compound_cross_reference: Magnoflorine (existing AISciMShub extraction) modulates Caspase-3 apoptosis downstream of neuroinflammation; candidate for TREX1/SAMHD1-deficient neuroinflammatory contexts.

compound_cross_references.bridge_relevance: Downstream of neuroinflammatory cascades driven by DDR-gene defects (e.g., TREX1, SAMHD1). The triangle query: given a synthetic lethal pair where one gene drives neuroinflammation, does Caspase-3 inhibition selectively rescue?
compound_cross_references.ddr_relevance: indirect — Caspase-3 is the executioner, not the DDR gene; but DDR defects that drive neuroinflammation converge on Caspase-3.

compound_cross_references.pathway_modulated: PARP1/2 single-strand break repair inhibition → synthetic lethal in HR-deficient backgrounds
compound_cross_references.bridge_relevance: PARP inhibitors are the clinical proof-of-concept for synthetic lethality. The DDR-Neuro bridge reframes them: which neurological contexts (BRCA2 carriers with cognitive decline, ATM heterozygotes) might benefit or be harmed?
compound_cross_references.ddr_relevance: direct — PARP1 is in the 233-gene screen; PARP inhibition is the canonical DDR-targeting therapeutic.

compound_cross_references.bridge_relevance: Oxidative stress is the dominant neurotoxic mechanism in NER-deficient neurons (Cockayne, XP). Hesperetin as an antioxidant is a candidate for ERCC6/ERCC8-deficient contexts.
compound_cross_references.ddr_relevance: indirect — targets the ROS elevation caused by NER failure.
